comment: Staleness stamps for the TLA+ models. Checked by tools/formalfresh (go test ./tools/formalfresh),
which runs inside `make test` and therefore inside `make ci`. It does NOT run TLC — it asserts that
the document sections each model was verified against are byte-identical to what they were at the
recorded run. TLC itself is `cd docs/formal && ./run.sh`, ~32 min and a JVM, which is why it is not in CI.
role=subject: the model ENCODES this section's machine. A change can invalidate the runs. Re-run ./run.sh.
role=premise: the correspondence map CITES this section to justify an encoding or a stated omission.
A change can invalidate a recorded justification without touching a single run. Re-read the row.
FM-7 is this repo's evidence for what a never-re-derived justification costs.
knownStale marks a section that HAS changed, with the task that owns re-verifying it — the
`[SPEC EDIT OWED]` pattern: marked, not absorbed. It is not an exemption. It pins the digest it is
stale AGAINST, so it covers exactly one known delta: a further edit to the same section fails again,
and a marker whose section matches its stamp once more is itself an error.
To restamp after a real re-run: make formal-restamp MODEL=<name>

subjects.why: added 2026-08-15 by #242, and RE-DERIVED at that moment rather than deferred — a re-read is the premise role's own remedy, and deferring one inside the mechanism built to prevent FM-7 would be FM-7. THE CLAIM THAT RESTS ON THIS SECTION is the FAIRNESS SET's first conjunct, AmbiguousOrder.tla's `\A i \in OrderIds : WF_vars((\E x : OrderFill(i,x)) \/ OrderFinal(i))`, recorded in the companion's §4 as 'the per-venue finality contract's own promise, per order slot: an order eventually executes or reaches a terminal status'. That promise is a claim about WHICH unresolved order states have an edge to a terminal, and §2 does not carry an order-state transition table — §2 NAMES the seven unresolved states in its `Ambiguous` row and §1 is the only place that says how each one leaves. P1–P4 are claimed only of fair behaviours, so this conjunct is not decoration: it is the premise the whole liveness half is conditional on. FOUR deltas since 310e854, not the two a reading of the version line suggests, and ALL FOUR either strengthen the premise or are already-recorded omissions — none narrows the edge set, and the diff contains no removed target anywhere. (1) v0.9.34 gave `Canceled` to both recovery query rows, five outcomes to six — the widening side of 'reaches a terminal status', for the answer §6 step 6's marketable IOCs make commonest. (2) v0.9.34 also gave the venue-initiated-termination row its explicit evidence rule (venue-terminal record PLUS the final executions sweep, never a status read alone); the model abstracts all four contract steps to one barrier and the map's 'one canonical boundary' row already states that as an abstraction boundary rather than a check, so this lands inside a recorded omission. (3) v0.9.36 added the stable-not-found ANCHOR to the `DispatchAuthorized` meaning row and to Invariants — a durability requirement on a timestamp, and §5's register records that this model has no real time. (4) #242 (v0.9.61) gave `Submitted` the query-resolution row it never had, and THAT ONE REPAIRS THE PREMISE: before it, §1 licensed no resolving exit for the state every successful `Place` lands on, and §1's own new paragraph states the consequence in this model's vocabulary — 'the order contributes a possible-delta interval for ever, §6.7 holds its hedge group `Ambiguous`', which is precisely the negation of `P1_AmbiguousEventuallyClassified`. So the fairness set was more generous than the spec licensed, on the commonest path, for four slices. Nothing green goes red: the 61 runs are unchanged and are now as strong as they were advertised to be. NO RE-RUN IS OWED and no map row needs re-deriving against the widened target set, because there is no such row to re-derive: neither .tla declares an order-state variable — §1's state names appear in both modules only in comments explaining what `orders[i].seen` abstracts — so nothing here reasons about which terminal a resolution reaches. This row is stamped fresh on the same footing as FenceTakeover's build-spec §6 and §7.5 rows: a premise re-derived, not re-run, with `verifiedCommit` left at 310e854 where it belongs.
